 On The 9 th Of April, 2025

 Umesh Bansal

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Samar Ghuraiya - Public Prosecutor for the State.
Shri Abhishek Parashar - Advocate for complainant.

Order 
This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of B.N.S.S/438 of Cr.P.C for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Crime No. 61 of 2025 registered at Police Station Porsa, District Morena (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 409 of IPC.
2.

The allegation against the applicant, in a nutshell, is that he committed cheating with complainants/victims thereby on the false promise of making them partners, he obtained huge amount of money from them.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the matter.
The transaction between the parties is of civil nature.
The complainant/victims have given total Rs.1.25 crores to the present applicant for having partnership in the sand business.

It is submitted that a lease deed was executed between Government of U.P.
and applicant and since the lease deed was executed in favor of an individual and partnership under the lease deed is not permitted, the contract of partnership could not take place, the present NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8224 2 MCRC-13915-2025 applicant has returned Rs. 9,50,000/- to the complainant/victims on different dates.
It is also submitted that the offence under Section 409 of IPC is also not made out against the applicant.

The complainant had sent a legal notice dated 08.09.2023, alleging that fraud has been committed against him and demanding the return of the money given by the complainant, the notice further states that if the money is not returned, an FIR will be filed at the concerned police station under Sections 420 and 409 of the IPC.
The contents of the notice clearly indicate that the matter is of a civil nature, therefore, present applicant deserves to be released on anticipatory bail.

To buttress his arguments, he relied on the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Naresh Kumar & Anr. v. State of Karnataka &
Umesh Bansal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99890314/
1 Anr. in a criminal appeal arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 1570/2021 .

entities.text:
Naresh Kumar & Anr. v. State of Karnataka &
Umesh Bansal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the complainant opposed the application.
5. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.

6 . A perusal of the aforesaid judgment in the case of Naresh Kumar (supra) reveals that the appellants therein had challenged the order dismissing their petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR.

In that case, the Apex Court found that the transaction was related as to how many bicycles had assembled and dispute between the parties was only regarding the figures of bicycles and the corresponding amount liable to be paid, which was a civil dispute, but the case in hand, however,
involves different factual circumstances and is distinguishable on facts from the aforesaid case.
Therefore, the aforementioned citation is of no help to the applicant.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the nature of the allegations leveled against the applicant,
this Court, without commenting on the merits of the case, is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:8224 3 MCRC-13915-2025 of the view that no case for the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant is made out.
7. Consequently, the present bail application is hereby dismissed.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE Aman Umesh Bansal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99890314/
